blind_spots.blind_spot: Claims 'mobile quantum computing' and portability with no SWaP-C specifics
blind_spots.operator_reality: Room-temperature qubits solve one lab constraint, but a system meant to ride on a vehicle or operator for GPS-denied navigation needs real power draw, weight, thermal, and ruggedization numbers — a bench prototype 'accessible and portable' in marketing terms is not the same as fieldable
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: site language stays at the physics-breakthrough level ('eliminates the need for extreme cooling') and never quantifies size, weight, power, or packaging
blind_spots.evidence_quote: propels quantum computing into a realm of unprecedented accessibility and portability

blind_spots.blind_spot: No ITAR/export-control awareness despite an EW/GPS-denied-nav application
blind_spots.operator_reality: Electronic warfare and PNT payloads are classic ITAR/export-controlled categories; a company whose public language talks about empowering 'individuals and industries' broadly, with no mention of controlled-technology handling, risks building an architecture that has to be re-engineered once export classification hits
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: mission language is aimed at commercial/academic accessibility, not defense-controlled deployment
blind_spots.evidence_quote: quantum computing is not confined to specialized laboratories but empowers individuals and industries to harness the immense computational power

blind_spots.blind_spot: Team page shows an entirely research-scientist bench, no integration/field/test engineers
blind_spots.operator_reality: A GPS-denied-nav payload destined for a vehicle or aircraft needs engineers who own vibration/shock qualification, platform power-bus integration, and GFE compatibility — a team of Scientist I/II and a Senior Quantum Scientist alone typically stalls exactly at the demo-to-fielded transition
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: leadership/technical team list is scientists and executives (CEO, COO, CFO, CTO, CIO) with no named deployment or hardware-integration engineer
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Sinan Bugu, Senior Quantum Scientist; Daniel Multer, Scientist II; Gabe Marcus, Scientist II; Scott McGuire, Scientist II

opener_hook: Your 2025 Navy Phase II SBIR is funding edge quantum processing for GPS-denied navigation — what's the SWaP-C budget for whatever it rides in?
what_they_do: Developing room-temperature, topological-material qubits for mobile/portable quantum computing, with DoD SBIR/STTR funding aimed at edge quantum processing for electronic warfare and GPS-denied navigation.
